['The mountain is harsh and the water is harsh, words cannot be spoken, a deep grudge arises, my heart burns like a winding river, and when I lose someone, I lose a part of myself too.  
When others lose someone, I lose someone as well. How could I not serve my husband faithfully despite this harsh fate?  
My poor husband, do not go—who will raise our young children? What sin do they bear in their youth? I just gaze up at the sky,  
thinking of my husband. When I think about it, I realized what my husband’s love truly was, but before I could fully understand, you passed away.  
How can I possibly raise this young, immature child alone? Ah, my grief…  
In this neighborhood alley, I wonder if my husband is here. Every day, whenever the sun rises, I think of my husband; even when looking at the moon, I think of him.  
I waited anxiously, hoping my husband would come home, but he has gone beyond this world. The cruel attachment remains even as I try to forget; no matter how much I steel my heart,  
your image from yesterday and today still appears vividly in my eyes.  
How could you leave me alone and go where you went?  
My in-laws complain morning and evening, my sister-in-law is troublesome, my brother-in-law is frantic,  
I carefully watch my behavior while trusting only my husband. With a single heart, I vowed to love you always,  
but why did you leave me and go beyond this world? Oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, my dear.  
If I had known you were going to leave me, I would have built a fortress at the edge of the world where you went,  
If I had known it would come to this, I would have called a shaman to perform rites and exorcisms, to try to save you.  
I never imagined you would go beyond this world. They say that place beyond is better than this life; if I had known,  
every morning and evening I would have drawn holy water and prayed with my hands clasped, asking my husband not to die.  
Why did you leave me so heartlessly? Even today, I think of you. On the cold winds of winter’s end and the snow-filled solstice,  
the west winds of Bukcheongsan blow fiercely downward. That harsh winter has passed, and spring has come.  
The nightingale sings lightly and deeply, crying, and the mountains and trees—even dead wood—revive, sprouting leaves and flowers,  
but when will my departed husband come? Without a word, you torment me so.  
It is frustrating and painful; I cannot speak of it before me. A deep grudge arises, my heart burns like a winding river.  
Coal, anthracite, bituminous coal, straw coal, bear’s fat—when burning, they produce smoke and steam, but my longing for my husband burns without any smoke or steam, only sorrow flows quietly like a droplet.  
Who understands this bruised liver? Oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, so dear, oh, my dear.', "In Muan land, the golden maiden

Name: 0_grandmother_mother law_sister law_father mother
Representative_Docs:
['At the field of Jangchan, when I tied my bundle and looked back,  
my waist did not ache.  
When I went into the house,  
the cold rice left from yesterday,  
even the plate soup was not finished,  
the cold soup left from yesterday  
was not even half finished.  
If asked to give dog meat, I gave dog meat,  
if asked to give chicken, I gave chicken,  
there was nothing left for my share to eat.  
The neighbor grandmother came to borrow firewood and said,  
"Chun-a, Chun-a, you fool Chun-a,  
how do you live eating this food?"  
"Grandmother, grandmother, please don’t say that,  
being born a woman,  
I’ve swept through the whole mixed yard."  
Listening carefully to grandmother’s words,  
holding a basket in one hand,  
a worn-out basket over my shoulder,  
a worn towel around my neck,  
with callused hands like a broom,  
with arms stretched out like a horsefly,  
I dusted myself off and left.  
The horse is going, the horse is going,  
the horse across is going,  
that bride going over there,  
is she a bride with a groom?  
She is so neat and pretty,  
they say she is a bride without a groom.  
I hold this walk,  
a bride without a groom,  
she just follows behind me.  
Going to follow behind her,  
in the twelve-room tiled house,  
there are many dogs that stand up,  
many that bark.  
Looking around the stable,  
there are many horses standing,  
many horses lying down.  
Entering the barn,  
there are many sheep and calves,  
and many cows and oxen.  
Entering the granary,  
there is rice stored for three years,  
trapping spiders in the nets,  
there is old sesame oil,  
three-year-old thick soy sauce.  
Entering the room,  
there are chamber pots and bucket stools,  
placed foot to foot,  
pillows set properly,  
everything arranged neatly.  
Stretching out and relaxing,  
this much is how I would live.  
I’m admiring my situation.  
Begging has come, begging has come,  
my real husband has come to beg.  
Jungjijong-a, come here,  
that woman over there is a beggar,  
don’t curse, give alms.  
Listen, my words,  
hear me just a little and leave.  
Where did you put your worn jacket?  
You came wearing old rags.  
Where did you put your straw mat?  
You are wearing shoes without heels.  
Where did you put your newly made gat (traditional Korean hat)?  
You came with an old rag hat.  
You may have a handkerchief in your hand,  
and you kick me with shoes on your feet.  
You may have a black spear,  
but you looked at me with a white spear.  
You came looking for me to beg.  
Don’t curse, step back.', 'My parents raised me with great care and affection.  
When it was time for me to join a good family, I went to live with my in-laws.  
The days were cold, the water was cold, and they told me to be careful.  
After only three days, they told me to go weed the fields.  
I refused, claiming it was a false accusation. Wearing ragged clothes,  
I held a hoe in my hand and went outside.  
There were many people at the house where I was married, so I couldn’t be seen.  
Without worry, I went outside and reached the East Sea.  
I was extremely fortunate; no matter how the winds shook from east, west, south, or north, I could not settle.  
I couldn’t distinguish right from wrong, but suddenly the workers  
chased me from all directions, saying this is my field, that is the field.  
When I crossed the field, the workers of that house followed me,  
searching the place around, hunting everywhere.  
Lightning flashed and I crossed that field.  
The front farm was my real field, and the back field was the one to be shared.  
I tried to weed by myself, and I was extremely fortunate.  
After I weeded the field alone, I weeded the rice paddies.  
I was thirsty and hungry, so I went to find Jeongshim Najal.  
Twelve people in the household had all eaten by then.  
I came to find Jeongshim Najal on account of the work.  
The old food was three-year-old barley rice,  
served in a bowl that was stained.  
The three-year-old kimchi stew was served in a dish.  
They threw food from ten miles away,  
some from five miles away, yet if I ate this rice,  
I’d choke and couldn’t swallow; I was hungry.  
I reluctantly ate the rice little by little.  
Then I saw Baekok Nangun, and when I opened the love gate and looked,  
Baekok Nangun said, “Are you leaving? Can’t you live here? Are you leaving?”  
Baekok Nangun said, “What’s this talk?  
We will live together for a thousand years; how can the parents die?”  
“Don’t go, don’t go, don’t leave me”—  
“We will live together for a thousand years; how can the parents die?”  
“Don’t go, don’t go; leave your worries and troubles behind.”  
Baekok Nangun said, “Look at my movement; bend twelve joints to support you.”  
I leaned on the wooden staff, but twelve joints broke.  
“Don’t mistake me for dead;  
although we have many partings,  
will we have more partings? This is the last word.”  
We parted with tears and I leaned on the wooden staff.  
I left the house through the gate,  
bowing deeply, walking slowly.  
As I walked, the wooden staff broke.  
Baekok Nangun ascended;  
she sat there, weeping loudly and bitterly,  
and then collapsed right there.', 'Three days after marriage, my sister-in-law, who picks cherries, urges me to weed the baby field.  
Look at the behavior of my mother-in-law.  
She washed her feet with cold water and urges me to weed the field.  
After weeding the first hill, then the second and third hills,  
it is almost lunchtime. As I arrive to have lunch,  
the sharp-tongued mother-in-law stirs her cold water feet.  
"Yesterday you came, my dear daughter-in-law, and today again, my dear daughter-in-law,  
what kind of work is this, coming only for lunch?"  
Hearing that voice, I was so overwhelmed that I couldn’t speak.  
Returning to my room, I tore seven pieces of cloth.  
I used two pieces to make a patchwork pouch, three pieces to make a bag,  
and one piece to make a simple sash, cutting and cutting,  
cutting my hair to look like a monk.  
I was going, but my husband said to go.  
He said he would ride a horse and go to the Seonbun family.  
Wearing half a plain sleeve, I turned around the side door.  
My husband said, "Dear, Shinjung family,  
don’t start any trouble with people.  
Dear, wearing half a plain sleeve,  
turn around the side door."  
At the end of his words, I suddenly grabbed his hand fiercely,  
trembling all over. "What’s wrong with you?  
What’s the matter with you, who usually wears a silk brocade waist bag?  
Why suddenly shave your head, who used to wear a golden hairpin and chop its hair?  
Why wear straw shoes over your worn shoes?  
Let’s go, let’s go back home."  
"I can’t go, I can’t go.  
Your parents' family is good, but I’m different, I have to go."  
Returning home, I asked my mother, "Where did he go?"  
"Since you left, he went away." The words made me so overwhelmed.  
Inside the three-foot coffin, inside the coffin, I cut my neck and died. / Sop'al']

The flagstone floor clatters,  
Feet want to dance,  
The room wants new clearing;  
The floor wants stomping,  
The wallsides want stepping.  
Dance, dance, Lutsu Mari.  
Do your feet work right away,  
Do handfuls of steps go through.  
Is the envelope round,  
Is the fabric half-length,  
Or are the little ones under wings,  
The rascals between belts.  
Slowly, slowly, wisely, wisely,  
Gently dance, young lady,  
Step beautifully.  
So the apron strings don’t snap  
Nor the too tight shoe straps.']

Name: 21_rooster_pillow_neck_handkerchief
Representative_Docs:
["At my parents' house, it used to be a rice tail and a tied bundle,  
but after a stranger came, it’s like dog food or acorn jelly,  
washed in water and plucked off, fluttering here and there,  
stirring me this way and that, am I a fighting rooster or a lost soul?  
Crying by day, crying by night.", 'When it’s a bit chilly, come into my arms,  
When the bamboo fence is tall, lean on my arms.  
With mandarin ducks, a golden hairpin, and a pine bamboo fence placed by the pillow,  
A brass chamber pot placed neatly by the bed.  
Looking up, there’s a conch shell tray; looking down, a patterned straw mat.  
On the patterned straw mat in the sleeping room’s floor—what’s going on?  
Why is there a pillow in the rice measuring box where you used to tuck your head?  
Why are there iron chains on the handcuffs you used to wear?  
Why is there a red hemp jeogori over the clothes you wore?  
Why is there a straw shoe for the sharp pointed shoes you used to wear?  
Oh, let’s live on with the sound of the side drum and the clatter of the earthenware jar.  
Oh, how good it is—this feeling I can’t deny.  
When is sleep ever at ease? Just now, I was blowing on it for warmth.  
Oh, this feeling—I cannot deny it.

— When playing, lamenting about fate?', 'Three-Character Phrase, Single-Wrapped Handkerchief  
Even if soaked like dew  
There is no one who knows me at all  
Buying a day without papers  
Placing it in front of the gate  
Where to go, not coming  
Clever rooster, don’t crow  
Barking dog, don’t bark  
It all hurts my heart  
Where has the beloved gone  
Will the barking dog not bark?  
Will the crying rooster not cry?  
In the market of life, roosters crow  
Living life,  
The black crow caws harshly  
Is today a far-off day?  
Tying the single-wrapped handkerchief  
Hanging it dripping  
My love, my dear love  
In the time of courting for a hundred years’ life  
Where has the promise gone?  
Leaving brothers and parents behind  
Leaving the Yangcheon parents beside  
Leaving the evergreen tree beside  
Promised to live a hundred years together  
No news from anywhere  
When the moon rises, I think  
When the sun sets, I think  
There is no dark night at all  
Suddenly and inexplicably  
The black crow caws harshly  
What news could come today?  
The crow caws joyfully  
The old color dims  
Looking at the world,  
On the way to Bodujip, as morning breaks  
Even if I starve from three meals and seven times  
The sound of the black crow’s cry  
Even happily, the hand goes away  
After making some noise  
The messenger came, the messenger came  
What messenger has come?  
Putting aside front and back doors  
I heard that the beloved is coming  
Even the dried-up rice is  
Salty but sweet  
No matter how much the Yangcheon parents  
Carefully arranged like young iron  
You said to live a hundred years  
Will this ever come true?  
The six children, sons and daughters  
What era will they face?']

Name: 22_father law_father_mother law_mother
Representative_Docs:
['When I said my mother-in-law died,  
I kept thinking about the barley room where I poured the water.', 'My mother died when I was one year old,  
My father died when I was two,  
I got married at three,  
When I opened the door to love,  
I found a tiger-like father-in-law,  
When I opened the door to the main room,  
I found a hen-like mother-in-law,  
When I opened the door to the back room,  
I found a quarrelsome sister-in-law.  
I wandered from room to room,  
Taking out twelve pieces of cloth,  
Seven pieces were folded,  
Four pieces were folded into a cone shape to make a hat,  
I go, I go, I am going,  
Grumbling, I am going.', 'I had a husband – oh dear God! Now I remember him every single moment. What a pity for my husband that I sadly lost him! He cut noodles, chopped grass, looked after the chickens, milked the cows. What a pity, etc. He swept the yard for me, chopped firewood, lit the stove, cleaned the pens. What a pity, etc. He carried water for me, cooked meals: yet he did not enjoy a good life with me. What a pity, etc. He spun thread for me, sorted the groats: and I told him, "You foolish fool!" What a pity, etc. I had pants and he had a skirt; that is why sad times came to me! What a pity, etc. I always had a husband according to my will: now I have a husband who beats me with a stick! What a pity for my husband that I sadly lost him!']

Name: 23_cheerful_village_forest_trees
Representative_Docs:
['Oh, what kind of village is this,
That is so merry?
All around it is green,
Inside it is joyful.
All around it is blooming viburnum,
Inside is the whole family.', 'One early morning,  
Very cheerfully went out in the lanes,  
As in such a merry forest,  
Built close by a city.  
It was a lovely wood,  
Planted with tall trees,  
A lovely sound,  
There the orchard resounded.', 'To Roosland zoo we sailed,  
And there indeed lived my sweet love, bis.  
Already for my sweet love behind the little door,  
And there stood two orchard trees, sweet. bis.  

On one hung a Nutmeg,  
On the other a Clove, sweet,  
I thought I was courting such a rich one,  
But alas, it was a poor blood. bis.  

I took her by her little hand,  
And I kissed her so red and so sweet, bis.  
And I courted her so lovingly and so far,  
Yes, all the way to under the Orchard. bis.  

The Orchard was closed,  
And indeed no one lived there, bis.  
Nothing but the sweet Nightingale,  
And it flew there down from above. bis.  

Now we will tie the Nightingale,  
With its head under its foot, bis.  
So that it won’t tell anyone,  
What is done under this Orchard. bis.  

Now we will end the song,  
Yes, in honor of the Bridegroom and Bride, bis.  
And then cheerfully, joyfully resound,  
And so we drink our glass out. bis.']
